title: Path integral control in the complex plane
abstract: Path integral control is a stochastic optimal control framework that computes optimal policies as weighted averages over state trajectories. It was recently shown that, combined with stochastic quantum trajectories, the path integral control approach constitutes a promising alternative for quantum optimal control. In this work, we propose an extension of path integral control to the complex plane using circular complex Wiener processes. The change of measure is defined on the driving noise space under an exact control-noise matching condition, which also accommodates rank-deficient state diffusions. Applied to stochastic Schrödinger equations, the resulting formalism gives a compact treatment of paired non-Hermitian jump channels with unequal positive dissipation rates and yields cross-entropy-optimal feedback and open-loop control formulas.
summary: This paper extends path integral control theory into the complex plane to develop a generalized framework for quantum optimal control. By minimizing the cross-entropy divergence, it derives explicit, optimal feedback and open-loop control laws for quantum systems. This method is particularly valuable for modeling complex open quantum systems with asymmetric dissipation rates.
main_problem: The paper extends path integral control theory, traditionally used for real-valued stochastic processes, to the complex plane to facilitate quantum optimal control.
main_result: The complex formulation provides a compact and structurally natural treatment for quantum systems, particularly those involving paired non-Hermitian jump channels with unequal dissipation rates.
method: It employs a variational approach minimizing the cross-entropy (CE) divergence, which is derived from a change of measure defined on the complex driving noise space.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to quantum systems governed by stochastic Schrödinger equations (SSE) and Lindblad master equations, covering single-qubit and two-qubit models with generalized amplitude damping.
key_observables: Cross-entropy-optimal feedback and open-loop control formulas, Lindblad fidelity, and the minimum cost related to the KL divergence.
important_parameters: Unequal positive dissipation rates, complex Wiener processes, and the structure of the control-noise matching condition.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the assumption that the infimum cost is attained and that the noise structure is restricted to circularly symmetric Gaussian distributions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the cross-entropy preparation of a specific quantum state using generalized amplitude damping, showing the evolution of Lindblad fidelity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from general path integral control theory to the complex extension, deriving variational forms for the reverse KL divergence, and then applying this formalism to solve for CE-optimal feedback and open-loop controls for specific quantum dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, mathematically rigorous framework for designing optimal quantum controls that naturally handles complex dynamics and asymmetric dissipation, which is crucial for modern quantum simulation and computation.
